provenance.notes: Mid-size pest operator with several branches, many technicians and a large recurring plan book, so the copy leans on plan checkout, the account portal, branch pages and commercial service records. Portal and integration ranges depend heavily on their routing and billing system; I set them wide.

pageStructurePlus.contains: One page per branch with its address, the towns its routes cover, the branch manager, local technicians, branch reviews and a [licence number] slot per branch
pageStructurePlus.why: Homeowners want the exterminator whose truck is already on their street. A branch page answers 'do you come here' and ranks for the town name.

pageStructurePlus.section: Pest plan comparison and online checkout
pageStructurePlus.contains: General, mosquito, termite and rodent plans side by side, what each visit includes, home size questions, card on file and a first visit picked from real route openings
pageStructurePlus.why: Plan buyers compare on what's covered and the monthly price. Letting them pay and pick a first visit online closes the sale without a call-centre queue.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Separate sections for food service, warehouses, hotels, offices and property portfolios, with inspection-ready service records, trap maps and a walkthrough request
pageStructurePlus.why: Facility and kitchen managers buy on audit readiness, not price. They need to see that records and corrective actions are part of the service.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Where plan customers see past visits, technician notes, invoices and the next scheduled treatment, request a re-service and update a card
pageStructurePlus.why: Plan customers cancel when they can't reach anyone. A visible login on the site tells a shopper the company is organised enough to keep them.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Open technician and inspector roles by branch, pay ranges the company chooses to publish, the paid training and licensing path, vehicle and tools provided, and a short application
pageStructurePlus.why: Technician hiring caps how many routes they can run. Applicants compare employers on training and the licence path before they apply.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How pre-construction termite treatment works for builders, scheduling against the pour, the paperwork handed over at closing, and a builder account request form
pageStructurePlus.why: Builders choose one termite vendor for a whole development. A dedicated page with a builder form turns that into a recurring account.

designDirections.name: Branch Near You
designDirections.bestFor: Regional pest companies whose first job is routing a searcher to the right branch and a booked first visit
designDirections.headlineSample: Pest control from the {City} branch, booked online today
designDirections.whyItFits: Steel Invoice's plain sans and crisp accent keep a branch finder, plan prices and a book button readable on a phone without decoration.

designDirections.name: Plan Checkout
designDirections.bestFor: Operators selling recurring home pest plans who want sign-up, payment and first visit done in one sitting
designDirections.headlineSample: Year-round pest plans in {City}, set up in minutes
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo fails CTA contrast. Evergreen Trust keeps a green feel with a button that passes, and its refined serif suits a plan people keep for years.

designDirections.name: Commercial Program Desk
designDirections.bestFor: Firms growing commercial accounts: kitchens, warehouses, hotels and property portfolios that buy on records
designDirections.headlineSample: Commercial pest programs for {City} kitchens and warehouses
designDirections.whyItFits: Gunmetal Signal's dark operations look and mono labels read like a service log, which suits facility managers who buy on records and audits.

openers.line: Your pest control site took a long while to load on my phone, and the plan prices sat below a large banner. Someone who just found droppings in the pantry won't wait for it.
openers.hook: Load their home page on a phone over mobile data and count roughly how long until the plan price or book button appears. Note it for the reply.
openers.linkLine: The same plans, loading fast on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Plan sign-up ends in a call
openers.line: Your site lists the home pest plans clearly, then every button says call us. Plenty of people would pay for the plan and pick a first visit right there if the page let them.
openers.hook: Click through their plan or pricing page and see whether a visitor can pay or book without a phone call. Note where the path ends.
openers.linkLine: Pest plan sign-up with payment and a first visit picked online: {demo-link}

openers.line: You run pest routes out of several branches, but the site has one contact page with a head-office number. A homeowner two towns over can't tell whether your technicians come to them.
openers.hook: Count the branches named on their listings or trucks, then check whether each has its own page with an address and towns covered.
openers.linkLine: A page for each pest control branch and the towns it covers: {demo-link}

openers.line: I've seen your posts hiring pest technicians at more than one branch, and the site has no careers page. Good applicants want to see the training and licence path before they apply.
openers.hook: Find a current technician or inspector job post on their social pages or a job board, note the branches, then check their site for a careers section.
openers.linkLine: A technician careers section with the licence path explained: {demo-link}

openers.line: Each of your pest control branches has its own run of reviews naming technicians, and none of them appear on the site. A shopper comparing exterminators never sees them.
openers.hook: Open two branch listings and copy one review line from each that names a technician. Quote one back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Branch reviews next to each pest plan: {demo-link}

openers.line: The pay-your-bill link on your site leads to a phone number. With a book of recurring pest plans, card updates and invoices are a big share of what your office answers.
openers.hook: Look for an account login, pay-a-bill or update-card link on the site. Note what it actually does when clicked.
openers.linkLine: A plan customer login for invoices, cards and re-service requests: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your commercial pest work is one paragraph on the services page. Kitchen and warehouse managers look for audit-ready records and trap maps before they ask for a walkthrough.
openers.hook: Find their commercial page or paragraph and check whether it mentions service records, industries served or a walkthrough form.
openers.linkLine: A commercial pest program page with records explained: {demo-link}

openers.line: When the weather warms and termite swarmers show up, every branch phone rings at once. An online inspection request that picks from real route openings takes the pressure off the office.
openers.hook: Use in the weeks before the local swarm season. Check their recent posts for swarmer or termite content.
openers.linkLine: Termite inspections booked online across branches: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your mosquito control program shows up in posts each season but has no page of its own. Families planning summer in the yard search for it by name and sign up early.
openers.hook: Search their posts for mosquito or yard treatments and check whether the site has a dedicated mosquito plan page with a price.
openers.linkLine: A mosquito control plan page with seasonal sign-up: {demo-link}

openers.line: Congratulations on the new branch. Right now the old company's pest control site and yours both show up for the same town, and customers aren't sure which one to call.
openers.hook: Only if they announced a new branch or an acquisition. Search the town name with pest control and note which sites appear.
openers.linkLine: One exterminator brand with the new branch folded in: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your termite customers renew every year, and the site has no way to renew, see the last inspection or pay online. That renewal letter is doing a lot of work on its own.
openers.hook: Check the termite page for any renewal, warranty-period or account wording. Note whether renewal is phone or mail only.
openers.linkLine: Termite renewal and inspection history online: {demo-link}

openers.line: People let an exterminator into the kitchen and the crawlspace, and they look for the licence. Your branches each carry one, and the site shows none of them.
openers.hook: Look for licence numbers on trucks, listings or the footer. Use only what they publish, in [brackets] on the demo.
openers.linkLine: Branch licence and insurance details beside each pest plan: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your branches close in the early evening, and the site only offers a phone number. Wasps by the front door and mice in the kitchen get found at night, and those people book whoever answers.
openers.hook: Call or check the hours on two branch listings. Note what a visitor can do on the site after closing.
openers.linkLine: After-hours pest requests booked into the next route day: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Dated next to the national brands
openers.line: Your crews and reviews are stronger than the national pest brands in your area, but the site looks a few years older than theirs. Plan shoppers judge the company by it.
openers.hook: Put their home page beside a national brand's on a phone. Note one concrete difference: no prices, small text, a stock bug photo.
openers.linkLine: Your exterminator brand, rebuilt to sit beside the national ones: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is the kind of pest control work facility and property managers want to see. It deserves a case page that leads to a commercial walkthrough.
openers.hook: Pick their newest commercial or large residential post: a restaurant, a warehouse, a termite job on a big property. Name it.
openers.linkLine: That pest job as a case page with a walkthrough request: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — I've been looking at how {Business Name} shows up across your branches.

The reviews are strong, but the site sends every plan shopper to a phone number, and there's no page per branch or way to pay for a plan online. I've put together a sample with plan checkout, branch pages and a customer login, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would it be useful if I sent it to you or whoever runs marketing?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case this got lost. Here's the sample site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has plan checkout with a first visit picked online, a page per branch with the towns it covers, a commercial program page and a customer login. Happy to walk your ops or marketing lead through it in fifteen minutes, or leave it there if the timing's wrong.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}. I build websites and customer portals for multi-branch pest control companies. I sent a sample site for {Business Name} a few days ago, did it reach you?"

IF NO:
"Short version: plan checkout with payment, a page per branch, a commercial program page and a login for plan customers, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Who should see it besides you?"

IF YES:
"What stood out?"
 → let them talk, then ask: "How do plan sign-ups and card updates reach your office today?"
"The site rebuild runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting, changes and reporting. For your branches I'd expect about {Build Price}. The portal and the routing-system connection are quoted separately once I see that system."
"Could we get thirty minutes with you and whoever owns operations next week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a short scope with the site first and the portal as phase two, so you can approve them separately."

objections.objection: Our routing software already has a customer portal.
objections.handler: "Then we connect to it rather than replace it. Most of those portals are hidden behind a plain login page nobody can find. I put the plan checkout and login on your site and pass the data to the system your office already runs."

objections.objection: We already pay a marketing agency.
objections.handler: "Keep them on ads and search. I build the parts agencies usually don't: plan checkout, branch pages tied to your routes and the customer login. They'll have a site that turns their traffic into plans."

objections.objection: I need to run this past the owner and operations.
objections.handler: "Makes sense. I'll send a one-page scope and a ten-minute walkthrough recording they can watch on their own time, and I'm happy to join a call with all three of you."

objections.objection: Branch managers won't keep their pages updated.
objections.handler: "They don't have to. Branch pages pull hours, reviews and towns from one place, and the care plan covers updates. A manager texts a change and it's done."

objections.objection: We might be acquired, so we're holding off.
objections.handler: "A clean plan book with online sign-ups and a customer login reads well in any sale conversation. I'd phase it so the site lands first and nothing locks you in."

objections.objection: How much for the whole thing?
objections.handler: "The site is {Build Range}, about {Build Price} for your branches, plus {Care Range} a month. The portal and integrations are a separate quote once I see your routing and billing setup."

email.subject: Plan checkout and branch pages for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build plan checkout, branch pages and customer logins for multi-branch pest control companies, and I made a sample for {Business Name}. I'll email the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm clearing out sample sites this week, including the {Business Name} pest control one with plan checkout and branch pages.

Should I keep it up for your operations or marketing lead to see? One word either way is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — termite and mosquito season is getting close in {City}, and that's when every branch phone rings at once. Thought of you.

The sample with plan checkout and branch pages is still here: {demo-link}. Same scope and price as before, whenever the timing suits.

bullets: Price against the plan book: the site only needs to add or keep a modest number of recurring plans across all branches to pay back.
Quote the site and the portal as separate phases; the portal depends on their routing and billing system and gets its own scope.
Branch pages are priced per branch, because each needs its own towns, reviews, hours and licence slot.
Commercial program pages earn more than home pages: price them on industries covered and the records explained.
Every line about products, safety or re-entry comes from labels and their own procedures, signed off by operations; bill the review time.
Never publish a licence or certification they haven't; leave a bracketed slot per branch.

Max with a builder account form, pour-date scheduling request and the closing paperwork explained.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile management for every branch
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each branch listing gets weekly posts of real pest work from its own routes, correct hours and answered questions, managed in one place."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests routed by branch and technician
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "After each pest visit the customer is asked to review the branch that served them, and managers see which technicians get named."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 1, once visit-complete data can be shared.

whatElseYouSell.name: Seasonal campaign set: termite, mosquito, rodent
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Three campaigns a year to past one-time customers and plan prospects by branch: termite inspections, mosquito sign-ups and rodent exclusion."
whatElseYouSell.when: Six weeks before each local pest season.

whatElseYouSell.name: Technician recruiting campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Recruiting posts and ads per branch that point to the careers page and the licence path, so route growth isn't stuck on hiring."
whatElseYouSell.when: Whenever they have open technician roles at more than one branch.

whatElseYouSell.name: Commercial capability pack
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short pest program document for kitchen and facility managers: industries served, service record samples and how audits are supported."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, before their commercial team's next bid season.

whatElseYouSell.name: Branch photo and video days
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A day at each branch filming technicians, trucks and exclusion work, so every branch page shows its own exterminators."

whatElseYouSell.name: Fleet lettering and branch signage artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Truck lettering and branch signs that match the new site and carry the plan sign-up address, coordinated with their sign shop."
whatElseYouSell.when: After launch, or when an acquired branch is rebranded.

whatElseYouSell.name: Monthly marketing report by branch
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One page each month: plan sign-ups, inspection requests and reviews by branch, so the general manager sees which pest routes are growing."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once the site has a full month of form data.

whatElseYouSell.name: Second-language plan and prep pages
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Plan pages, treatment prep sheets and checkout in a second language your customers and technicians use, approved by operations."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, where branches serve communities that prefer another language.

withoutAI.route: Property management firms on their commercial routes
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The property managers whose buildings your technicians treat every month still take maintenance requests by email. Introduce me and I'll show them a resident request page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Managers trust the pest vendor who keeps tenants quiet, and that trust gets a meeting with the person who buys software.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The restaurant group on your commercial pest route still posts PDF menus for each site. Your service manager sees their ops director more than anyone."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Restaurant operators trust the vendor who keeps them inspection-ready, and multi-site groups all need ordering and location pages.

withoutAI.route: Home builders using their termite pretreatment
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The builder who books your termite pretreatment on every slab shows each community as a PDF. Community pages with lot maps are the next build."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Builders rely on the pest company at every pour; the introduction comes from a vendor they already schedule weekly.

withoutAI.route: Hotels and serviced apartments on contract
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The hotel you treat for bed bugs and roaches runs its direct bookings through a dated page. Your account manager can open that door."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Hospitality managers share their worst problems with their pest vendor, so a referral from them carries weight.

withoutAI.whoPays: The wildlife company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "When your branches get raccoon, bat or pigeon calls, who gets the referral? That wildlife operator needs an urgent request page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Pest and wildlife companies pass jobs both ways every week, so the handoff is natural.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The food warehouse on your commercial pest route schedules dock appointments by phone. A carrier booking page would save their yard team hours."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Warehouse managers already trust the vendor who keeps their audits clean; that trust reaches the operations director.

withAI.route: Resident request sorter for property managers
withAI.pitchLine: "Resident messages about roaches, mice or leaks get sorted by building and urgency, and pest work orders go straight to the exterminator's branch."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers spend mornings forwarding complaints, and the pest client gets cleaner work orders back.

withAI.pitchLine: "Each kitchen manager asks what the last pest visit found and what's open before an inspection, and gets answers from the service records across every site."
withAI.whyItWorks: Groups dread inspections across many kitchens, and the pest client already produces the records.

withAI.route: Buyer question assistant for home builders
withAI.pitchLine: "Home buyers ask about lots, finishes and the termite pretreatment paperwork, and the builder's sales team gets the warm leads with answers attached."
withAI.whyItWorks: Builders field the same buyer questions all day; the pest client's paperwork is one of them.

withAI.pitchLine: "Guest complaints that mention bugs are flagged by room and sent to housekeeping and the pest vendor before the review gets written."
withAI.whyItWorks: Hotels fear the bed bug review more than the bill, and the pest client gains faster calls.

withAI.pitchLine: "Callers describe the noise in the roof, and likely rodent jobs go to the pest branch while raccoons, bats and birds go to the wildlife crew."
withAI.whyItWorks: Both companies get cleaner calls, and the pest client gets the rodent exclusion work back.

withAI.route: Sanitation log drafter for food warehouses
withAI.pitchLine: "Supervisors talk through the sanitation walk and get a drafted log, with pest findings pulled from the exterminator's latest service record."
withAI.whyItWorks: Warehouses write these logs daily, and the pest vendor's data is already half of what they need.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call and form text-back to the nearest branch
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A missed call or web form gets a text within a minute with the right branch's plan prices and a link to book, so the lead isn't lost while the office is busy."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 1. Needs the branch phone numbers forwarded, town-to-branch mapping and approved wording.

softwareAI.name: Failed card recovery for plan payments
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a recurring pest plan payment fails, the customer gets a polite text and email with a secure card update page before the office has to chase it."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs access to the billing system's failed-payment report and the wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Online plan checkout connected to the routing system
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner picks a pest plan, pays, and chooses a first visit from real route openings, and the account appears in your routing system without retyping."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the routing and billing system's connection details, plan rules by branch and a test account.

softwareAI.name: Website assistant for plan and pest questions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'do you cover my town' and 'what does the termite plan include' from your own plan terms, then books the first visit. It never gives safety advice."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs plan terms, the town-to-branch list and approved wording. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Plan customer portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Plan customers log in to see visit history, technician notes and invoices, request a re-service and update a card, with everything synced to the routing system."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3 to month 5. Needs the routing and billing system's data access, a customer export and the re-service policy.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for every branch
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each new branch review gets a drafted reply naming the pest job and technician, waiting for the branch manager to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside the review requests. Needs branch listing access and a tone guide. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Branch growth dashboard
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Plan sign-ups, cancellations, re-services and reviews per branch on one screen, so the general manager sees which pest routes grow and which leak."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a few months of site data and an export from the routing and billing system.

softwareAI.name: Termite renewal reminders with online payment
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Termite customers get renewal notices ahead of the date with a pay-online link and their last inspection summary, so fewer renewals lapse."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the termite account list, renewal terms and the billing connection.

softwareAI.name: After-hours phone assistant across branches
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Evening callers about wasps, mice or termite swarmers reach an assistant that takes details, finds their branch and books the next route opening."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs branch calendars, services by branch and approved urgent-call wording. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Commercial client portal with service records
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Kitchen and facility managers log in to download pest service records, trap maps and corrective actions for each site before an audit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the service log data, commercial account list and the record formats their clients' auditors expect.

softwareAI.name: Technician applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for pest technician roles answer questions about driving, crawlspaces and the licence exam, and each branch manager gets a ranked shortlist."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any month they're hiring at more than one branch. Needs must-haves, pay bands and the training plan. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: New technician licensing tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every new exterminator's training hours, ride-alongs, exam date and licence renewal in one place, so no technician runs a route out of compliance."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the training checklist, licence renewal rules where they operate and the technician roster.

softwareAI.name: Visit summary writer for plan customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Technician notes turn into a plain visit summary for the customer: areas treated, what was found, prep for next time, approved wording only."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs sample technician notes and the approved label and prep wording. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Cancellation save flow
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a plan customer cancels online, they're offered a free re-service or a plan change first, and the branch sees the reason the same day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, after the portal. Needs the retention offers operations will honour and cancellation reasons.

softwareAI.name: Route density map for door-to-door sales
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Streets where you already treat several homes light up on a map, so sales reps knock where an extra pest plan adds no drive time."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs plan addresses and route days by branch.

softwareAI.name: Inbound message triage across branches
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Emails, texts and web messages get sorted into re-service, billing, new plan and commercial requests, routed to the right branch with a draft reply."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the shared inboxes, the text line and routing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Acquired customer list onboarding tool
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When you buy a smaller exterminator, its customer list is cleaned, matched to routes and invited to the portal with a welcome note from the new branch."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: When they next acquire. Needs the acquired company's customer export and the plan mapping operations decides on.

softwareAI.name: Pest photo triage for incoming requests
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner uploads a picture of the insect or droppings, and the branch sees a likely pest and suggested visit type to confirm before calling back."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs past requests with photos and what each turned out to be. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Procedure assistant for technicians
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A technician on a route asks how the company handles a bed bug job or a crawlspace entry and gets the written procedure, with label references, not a guess."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs written procedures and operations' sign-off on every answer. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Commercial walkthrough quoting app
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Commercial reps walk a kitchen or warehouse with a tablet, log devices and risk areas, and leave with a priced pest program proposal ready to send."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs their commercial pricing rules, device types and proposal template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the plan checkout for regional pest operators
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Pest control companies, monthly per branch
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built plan checkout tied to the routing system for one multi-branch exterminator. Every regional operator loses plan sales to a phone queue."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client paid for the integration work, which every company on the same routing system shares.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every pest operator who buys from you branch pages, plan checkout and service records as a member tool, and they keep ordering through you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors compete for mid-size operators, and a daily tool holds an account better than a rebate.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "For operators growing past one branch, the association hands out a ready branch-page and checkout system, with wording reviewed so no member strays into treatment claims."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations want compliant marketing for members, and one agreement reaches many owners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The platform company, per acquired brand
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each exterminator you acquire keeps its local name. One site system, one checkout and one portal template, rolled out to every new brand in weeks."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Roll-ups buy local brands constantly and need them rebuilt quickly and consistently.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label for agencies serving pest companies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency runs ads for pest operators but sends traffic to sites that can't take a plan payment. License my checkout and branch-page system."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies keep the client relationship; you sell the part that's hard to build.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Facility management companies' vendor records hub
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Pest records, trap maps and corrective actions from every vendor across every site you manage, collected in one place before audits."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Facility managers chase vendor paperwork across many buildings, and the pest client already produces the records in the right shape.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every property's pest incidents, room holds and treatments on one board, so the group sees problems before guests write about them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Hotel groups need consistent records across properties, and the pest client's data starts it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The pest program section of your food safety audit, kept current from your exterminator's records instead of rebuilt in a binder each time."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Food plants buy on audit readiness, and the pest client already visits them on a fixed schedule.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every lot's termite pretreatment certificate filed and handed to the buyer at closing from one portal, across all your communities."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders need the paperwork on every closing, and the pest client already produces it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each franchisee gets territory pages, plan checkout and a portal on one brand system, built once and copied per territory."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Franchisors need consistent local pages for every territory; the multi-branch build is the same shape.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: The same branch system for the next regional operator
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A non-competing pest company in another region
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I work with one multi-branch exterminator per region, and {City} is taken. The next region over is open, and the plan checkout is already built."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the checkout, the portal and the case study.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The pest company with an unfinished build
